metadata.title: How to Learn Anything Faster
metadata.description: An illustrated guide to active recall, deliberate practice, and a learning loop you can use today.

hero.label: A field guide to learning
hero.intro: Turn what you read, watch, and hear into a skill you can actually use.
hero.alt: An open book whose pages become blue steps, with a yellow pencil across the page.

trap.label: The learning trap
trap.title: Knowing is only the beginning.
trap.intro: A book, a tutorial, or a page of highlighted notes can make a topic feel familiar. The test is what you can do with it.
trap.alt: On the left, a learner sits among books and tutorials. On the right, they assemble a wooden stool.
trap.habitRead: Reading books and rarely applying the lessons.
trap.habitWatch: Watching tutorials without trying the technique.
trap.habitCollect: Collecting information you struggle to recall.
trap.takeaway: Real learning begins when you do something with what you know.

recall.label: Active recall
recall.title: Test yourself.
recall.intro: Close your notes and try to retrieve the idea from memory. That effort helps you bring it back when you need it.
recall.exerciseAnswer: Answer questions with your notes closed.
recall.exerciseFlashcard: Use flashcards to test key concepts.
recall.exerciseRevisit: Revisit difficult ideas at increasing intervals.
recall.prompt: What do you remember without looking?
recall.answer: After a chapter, close the book. Explain its main idea in your own words, then open it again to see what you missed.

practice.label: Practice
practice.title: Turn knowledge into action.
practice.intro: Pick a small task that lets you use the thing you just learned.
practice.alt: Hands with a pencil and notebook fit a wooden piece into a project on a worktable.
practice.businessText: Study a problem and develop a solution.
practice.takeaway: Start with a small exercise, get feedback, then gradually increase the difficulty.

simulation.label: Simulate reality
simulation.title: Practice for the real thing.
simulation.intro: Make your practice resemble the situation in which you’ll actually use the skill.
simulation.rehearseAlt: A person rehearses a talk from their notes at a desk.
simulation.performAlt: The same speaker delivers a talk to three people at a small lectern.

loop.title: The learning loop.
loop.intro: Use this cycle to turn one important idea into a skill. Then repeat.
loop.recallText: Close your notes and explain what you remember.
loop.applyText: Use the concept in a real task or practical exercise.
loop.reflectText: Identify what went wrong, get feedback, and improve.

today.title: Put it to work today.
today.intro: After your next book, course, podcast, or tutorial, ask yourself three questions.
today.second: Can I explain it without looking?
today.third: How can I apply it today?
